title: Independent-encryptor audit: 678 K4-shaped messages from textbook encryptors (no shared code) fed to the test functions of attacks 63, 66, 71, 72, 74, 78
k4_result: Not applicable: this idea makes no claim about K4 and decrypts nothing. Basics all agree (16/16 checks): K4 in data/ equals a hand-typed K4, carved rows are 4+31+31+31, letters 22-34 and 64-74 are FLRVQQPRNGKSS and NYPVTTMZFPK, kryptos.CRIBS and the POS/B1/B2/WORDS lists of rounds 9 and 11 are the same 24 positions. The textbook strip encryptors turn the K1 and K2 plaintexts into the carved ciphertext (PALIMPSEST, ABSCISSA; K2 both as carved and with the S restored) and rebuild the 26 carved tableau rows.
controls: Shuffled K4s do not apply (no K4 score to compare). Two controls of the audit itself: (1) a planted mistake, 30 messages with the clue words one letter late given to attacks 63 and 66 as if correctly placed: 0 found, as it must be; (2) 40 decoy alphabets handed over with each true one: a decoy setting was listed for 3 of 606 messages.
planted: 560/678 found; 3 more had too few checks to be judged (plain-feed keyed-lag autokey); 115 missed with enough checks, all in attack 66. By attack: 63 48/48; 66 323/438; 71A 24/24; 71B 60/60; 72 48/48; 74 22/24 (2 unjudgeable); 78 (tests 68, 71B, 74 on column-mixed alphabets) 35/36 (1 unjudgeable). Attack 66 without the two hole kinds below: 323/323.
scope_limits: Audits only the test functions of attacks 63 (search), 66 (work), 71 (pairs_search, work), 72 (fixed_rules, work_words, work_keys), 74 (test_view, work) and 78 (tests 68 clue-1-alone, 71B, 74 through kryptos.idea78_mixed); not test 70, not the gap-slack part of 68, not attacks 54-62, 67, 69, 73, 75-77, 79-90, and not the English-scoring stage of any attack. 6 messages per model (113 models), random in-scope settings, true alphabet handed over with 40 decoys rather than the full 667,000-alphabet list (the planted alphabets were checked to be in each attack's own list: 0 missing). Alphabets come from 46 audit words. It shows the conventions agree with textbook definitions and with K1/K2 as carved; it cannot show that K4 uses any of these ciphers.

negative.family: Method audit (shared conventions in planted tests)
negative.hypothesis: The exact clue tests of rounds 9-11 share a convention mistake with their own planting code (clue positions off by one, an alphabet indexed the wrong way, a Beaufort sign), so they pass their planted tests and would still miss the real K4.
negative.scope: Textbook encryptors written from the definitions with no code from kryptos/ (checked against the carved K1, K2 and tableau): Quagmire I-IV in Vigenere and Beaufort form with any index letter, sliding key, progressive key, autokey (plain and cipher feed), two stacked keys, multiplier + adder words, fixed multiplier + key, paper rotor (8 turning rules), keyed-lag autokey; plain and column-mixed keyword alphabets; 678 K4-shaped messages (EASTNORTHEAST at 22-34, BERLINCLOCK at 64-74) through the test functions of attacks 63, 66, 71, 72, 74, 78.
negative.outcome: Dead: no convention mistake. Positions, alphabets, index letter and Beaufort sign all agree; attacks 63, 71, 72, 74 and 78 found every judgeable planted message (237/237, 3 unjudgeable) and attack 66 found 323/323 inside what it really tests (controls: 30 messages with the clue one letter late, 0 found; shuffled K4s do not apply; planted 560/678 overall). But two scope holes in attack 66 and kryptos.round11.battery: (a) 'two stacked keys p<q<=13' is only tested at 21 of the 41 length pairs that have 7+ checks; a quick pre-filter wrongly drops (3,11) (3,13) (4,11) (4,13) (5,9) (5,11) (5,12) (5,13) (6,9) (6,10) (6,11) (6,13) (7,8) (7,9) (7,10) (7,11) (8,9) (8,10) (8,12) (9,12), so K4 was never tested there on dictionary tableaux; (b) autokey is only tested with the feed letter numbered on the keyword alphabet M, so the usual Quagmire I autokey (M/AZ, M/KR with the key letter on the cipher strip), its mirror on AZ/M and KR/M, and rows picked by A-Z label on M/M are untested (90/90 missed), as is a progressive key moved on in A-Z order.

follow_ups: Close hole (a): two stacked repeating keys on every dictionary keyword tableau (5 layouts, Vigenere/Beaufort) at the 20 length pairs the pre-filter in attacks/66 battery() and kryptos/round11.battery() wrongly drops: (3,11) (3,13) (4,11) (4,13) (5,9) (5,11) (5,12) (5,13) (6,9) (6,10) (6,11) (6,13) (7,8) (7,9) (7,10) (7,11) (8,9) (8,10) (8,12) (9,12). The filter adds two partial counts (c1 + c2 < 8) that are not the number of exact checks; replace it by the exact mod-13/mod-2 solve (attack 66's _stacked_exact already accepts all 20). Planted test: kryptos.idea91_audit.Audit.stacked_map must find 41 of 41. The same fix applies to the stacked rule inside attacks 68, 70, 71B, 78, 81, 88.

Close hole (b): autokey on every dictionary keyword tableau where the feed letter is numbered on an alphabet other than M: A-Z, KRYPTOS, or the other side's alphabet (Quagmire I autokey as the ACA defines it: key letter found on the straight cipher strip; rows picked by the A-Z labels as on the carved tableau). Lags 1-6, plain and cipher feed, both signs, 5 layouts, Vigenere/Beaufort: each test fails after about two comparisons, so all 667,000 alphabets take minutes. Add the progressive key moved on in A-Z order. Planted test: the idea-91 cells 'autokey ..., key letter on the cipher strip [M/AZ]' and '... picks the row by its A-Z label [M/M]'.

Run the same audit on the attacks it did not reach: rounds 9-10 (54-62, 65, 67), 69, 70, 73, 75-77 and the swarm attacks 79-90. kryptos/idea91_textbook.py already has the encryptors for most of them; each needs a 20-line plant_NN in kryptos/idea91_audit.py. Check first every attack that says 'p < q <= 13' or 'autokey' in its negative, since the two holes found here may repeat.
